title: the WSG mounts and beasts of burden chapter slice - the full catalog of land-based animals as mounts and pack animals with the animals-as-individuals rules, the Table 42 reaction grid and the calming and understanding rules, printed pp. 90-94, CLOSING the mounts and beasts of burden chapter
audit_label: R490 WSG mounts and beasts pin audit
audit_comment: The mounts and beasts of burden chapter, CLOSING it. The catalog: the gorilla - highest intelligence, befriended and trained for instructions and transport, the point man, no stealth with the at-least-1-in-6 surprise cut, the 50-degree floor, the 50-50 lethargic-or-aggressive desertion on prohibited terrain, 10x food (plants) and 8x water with the 25 percent foraging no-return; the brown bear - magic to carry reliably, the 30 percent monthly nonmagical reversion, any terrain but swamp and desert, claw sure-footedness against smooth inclined slopes, omnivorous, 8x food and 6x water; the camel - the dromedary hot-desert exclusive with no mountains, forests or swamps and no severe slope, weak below 50 degrees for over two days, the bactrian smaller feet on rocky ground, the two-week fast off the humps with the second-week half capacity and the two-week feeding deadline, the empty camel at 10x food and 20x water reduced proportionately after a shorter fast; the sled dog - the 40-degree ceiling with 2-3 inches of snow, a man's ration daily, the two-day cannibalism bar at 50 percent with the preemptive cull, the seven-dog optimum with the 200 and 300 gold piece losses per dog short and the 3-inch rate cut per three dogs short, the four-dog 9/6/3 rates and the single-dog 6/3 with the rugged ban; the donkey as the mule; the elephant - trained only on command words, the 50-degree floor, no severe slope without a level pass, the 3-inch forage slowdown, fifty food and thirty water rations, the 50-percent-every-six-hours bolt after two unfed days; the horse - the fragile overloaded exception with the one-turn rest per six turns, the half-ration bit with the unloaded back, the 2 percent lame chance per eight rugged hours (1 for the draft) with the 01 temporary at 12 hours of rest and the 02 permanent, four food and four water rations; the mule - hardier but slower, the half-hour stubborn root with the Strength Check and the three-fourths rations for three days; the pony - the horse statements, the mountain breeding, the 2 percent lame per eight hours, three rations; the giant ram - the trained charge, the 70-degree ceiling, the flat dry persuasion but no forests or swamps, 6 food and 4 water rising to 6 water above the 50-degree daily high; the sheep - the two-dozen capacity, no proficiency to shepherd, six per handler with another per additional six, the 50-percent-per-hour unsupervised bolt, the 70-degree ceiling, 2 food and 2 water, the nondurable-supplies food value; the yak - the ram-like mountainous arctic exclusive at the 30-degree ceiling, 6 food and 4 water. Animals as individuals: bit players or unique non-player characters, the reputable former-owner information, the sure-footed hates-wet-feet example, the wild-captured trial and error, the controlled exposure, calmness and stability, the instinctive fire fear with the innate weather sense, the acute smell and hearing with the not-capricious note. Table 42: the 14-animal reaction grid on 1d12 across fire, weather, noise, odor and other - leftmost noticed, second agitated, third panicked, the bare trailing slash pinned as the sentinel 13 meaning no panic. The bands: the two-round calm window, the trust-the-instinct advice, the panicked irrational flight uncontrollable for 2d3 turns or until far enough away, the fire commentary with the lava and magical-heat extension and the faerie fire exception, the campfire association, the never-comfortable-near-large-blaze rule, the quarter-mile large-blaze and one-mile conflagration sensing, the weather sense with the drastic-and-imminent panic bar, the noise habituation with the simulated combat training, the sharp hearing that never panics at the inaudible, the odor pungency bar with the faint-odor exception, and the other-quirk menagerie. Calming: anyone may try, the proficient with above-average wisdom every round, the nonproficient straight 20 percent with two attempts, movement only while calming, the motion-state persistence with the 50-50 split, the soothe-a-mover requirement, the agitated and panicked proficient-only with the +2 and +4 modifiers, and the re-excitement under an evident condition. Understanding: the animal lore educated guess, the nonproficient sensory guesswork, and the proficient certainty that rules out the rest.

banner.title: R490: the WSG MOUNTS AND BEASTS OF BURDEN chapter slice, printed pp. 90-94 - the round CLOSING the chapter: the twelve-animal catalog from the ape and the bear through the yak with every terrain bar, temperature floor and ration multiplier, the animals-as-individuals personality rules, the Table 42 1d12 reaction grid across fire, weather, noise, odor and other with the noticed-agitated-panicked bands and the two-round windows, the fire and weather and noise and odor commentary, and the calming and understanding rules - the magic in the wilderness chapter rides to R491.
banner.provenance: THE SETTLE: the catalog pages two-way clean - the pdftotext layout reads and the tesseract tsv reconstructions agree on every number (the ape 1-in-6 and 50 degrees and 50 percent and 10x and 8x and 25, the bear 30 and 8x and 6x, the camel 50 degrees and two days and two weeks and the half capacity and 10x and 20x, the dog 40 degrees and 2-3 inches and two days and 50 percent and seven and 200 and 300 and the 3-inch step and the four-dog 9/6/3 and the single-dog 6/3, the elephant 50 degrees and the 3-inch slowdown and fifty and thirty and two days and 50 percent every six hours, the horse one turn per six and the half-ration bit and the 2 percent per eight hours and the draft 1 percent and 01 at 12 hours and 02 permanent and the four and four rations, the mule half an hour and the three-fourths for three days, the pony 2 percent and three rations, the ram 70 degrees and 6 and 4 rising to 6 above the 50-degree high, the sheep two dozen and six per handler and 50 percent per hour and 70 degrees and the 2 and 2, and the yak 30 degrees and 6 and 4). The Table 42 garbles settled: the layout 8110112 class is 8/10/12 with the slash rendered as a one, the ampersand and copyright glyphs in the camel and donkey other cells are both 6, and the two-number cells print a bare trailing slash after the agitated number - pixel-identical to the interior slash - meaning no third number and no panic, pinned as the sentinel 13. The MULE ROW defeated tesseract outright (confidence 0.0 on two cells, the row prints in lighter ink) and pdftotext dropped the horse-other, mule and pony rows entirely: settled by a template glyph pass on the 300-dpi png - digits and slashes harvested from the same table's confidently-read cells, matched at the light-ink thresholds - giving fire 6/11, weather 6/12, noise 6/11, odor 7/12 and other 6/10/12, agreeing with every tesseract fragment it did manage. The elephant noise cell initially misread from its row-rule contamination and re-settled to 8/12 on the proper band. Book typos: greater that that, geta, eal, occurin, 1in 6. The reaction, calming and understanding prose two-way clean (1d12, two rounds, 2d3 turns, one-quarter and one mile, 20 percent and two attempts, the 50-50 motion split, +2 and +4).
banner.sentinel: Bounds held: every Table 42 cell ascends noticed to agitated to panicked, the sentinel 13 appears only in panic columns (one in fire, three in weather, three in noise, two in odor, none in other), the donkey row is uniform 4 or 6 over 10 over 12, the mule carries four sentinels with its full other band, the panic modifier doubles the agitated modifier, the bear reverts at 30 percent while the ape splits 50-50, the dog team loses 200 and 300 gold pieces per dog short with the 3-inch rate cut per three dogs, the horse lame 01 recovers at 12 hours while 02 is permanent, the ram water rises from 4 to 6 above the 50-degree daily high, the sheep handler step matches the control count at six, and the yak is the coldest at 30 degrees.

consts.name: wmbApeSurpriseMin
consts.comment: the surprise reduction should be at least 1 in 6, perhaps greater in certain circumstances

consts.name: wmbApeMinTempF
consts.comment: gorillas can be persuaded to serve as pack animals in any forest, hills or plains area where the effective temperature does not drop below 50 degrees

consts.name: wmbApeDesertChancePct
consts.comment: the lethargic-or-aggressive split on prohibited terrain: a 50 percent chance of either

consts.name: wmbApeFoodMult
consts.comment: a gorilla requires ten times as much food as a man does on a daily basis to maintain full strength and vitality - plants will suffice, since gorillas are primarily herbivorous

consts.name: wmbApeWaterMult
consts.comment: a gorilla requires eight times as much water as a man does on a daily basis

consts.name: wmbApeForageFailPct
consts.comment: if allowed to hunt and forage for itself, there is a 25 percent chance every time it goes out that it will not return

consts.name: wmbBearRevertPct
consts.comment: the non-magical bear reversion chance: 30 percent per month

consts.name: wmbBearFoodMult
consts.comment: a bear needs eight times as much food as a man does to maintain full strength

consts.name: wmbBearWaterMult
consts.comment: a bear needs six times as much water as a man does to maintain full strength

consts.name: wmbCamelMinTempF
consts.comment: the dromedary becomes weak and lethargic if forced to be exposed to temperatures lower than 50 degrees

consts.name: wmbCamelWeakDays
consts.comment: the dromedary weakens when exposed below its temperature floor for more than two days in a row

consts.name: wmbCamelMaxDepriveWeeks
consts.comment: a camel of either sort can go for up to two weeks without eating or drinking, living off the water and nutrients stored in its hump or humps

consts.name: wmbCamelDeprivedCapPct
consts.comment: the second-week carrying capacity: one-half of normal

consts.name: wmbCamelFeedWeeks
consts.comment: the animal must be fed and watered at least once every two weeks, or at the end of that period its condition will rapidly deteriorate

consts.name: wmbCamelEmptyFoodMult
consts.comment: an empty camel needs ten times as much food (plants) as the daily ration for one man

consts.name: wmbCamelEmptyWaterMult
consts.comment: an empty camel needs twenty times as much water as the daily ration for one man

consts.name: wmbDogMaxTempF
consts.comment: the sled and its dogs are only usable when the temperature is lower than 40 degrees

consts.name: wmbDogSnowMinIn
consts.comment: the ground must have at least a significant amount of snow cover - the minimum: 2 inches

consts.name: wmbDogSnowMaxIn
consts.comment: the significant snow cover range: 2-3 inches

consts.name: wmbDogStarveDays
consts.comment: if sled dogs are forced to go for more than two days without solid food, the cannibalism risk begins

consts.name: wmbDogCannibalPct
consts.comment: there is a 50 percent chance on each day after the starvation threshold that the stronger members of the group will kill and eat one or two of the weaker ones

consts.name: wmbDogTeamFull
consts.comment: the optimum number of dogs pulling a sled is seven

consts.name: wmbDogNormalLossGp
consts.comment: for every dog less than the optimum number, the normal-load encumbrance limit for the team is reduced by 200 gold pieces

consts.name: wmbDogMaxLossGp
consts.comment: for every dog less than the optimum number, the maximum-load encumbrance limit is reduced by 300 gold pieces

consts.name: wmbDogRateStepDogs
consts.comment: for every three dogs less than the optimum, all movement rates are reduced

consts.name: wmbDogRateLossIn
consts.comment: the movement rate loss per three dogs short: 3 inches

consts.name: wmbDogFourNormalIn
consts.comment: the four-dog sled normal-load rate on normal terrain: 9 inches

consts.name: wmbDogFourFullIn
consts.comment: the four-dog sled full-load rate on normal terrain: 6 inches

consts.name: wmbDogFourRuggedIn
consts.comment: the four-dog sled normal-load rate over rugged terrain: 3 inches

consts.name: wmbDogOneNormalIn
consts.comment: the single-dog sled normal-load rate on normal terrain: 6 inches

consts.name: wmbDogOneFullIn
consts.comment: the single-dog sled full-load rate on normal terrain: 3 inches

consts.name: wmbEleMinTempF
consts.comment: an elephant can only be used in a climate where the temperature does not drop below 50 degrees

consts.name: wmbEleForageSlowIn
consts.comment: the foraging elephant moves 3 inches slower

consts.name: wmbEleFoodRations
consts.comment: if food and water are not readily available, an elephant must be fed the equivalent of fifty food rations each day to maintain full strength

consts.name: wmbEleWaterRations
consts.comment: the daily water requirement for a non-foraging elephant: thirty water rations

consts.name: wmbEleBoltDays
consts.comment: an elephant forced to travel for more than two days without getting its full rations risks bolting

consts.name: wmbEleBoltCheckHours
consts.comment: the bolt check: every six hours

consts.name: wmbEleBoltPct
consts.comment: there is a 50 percent chance on each bolt check that the elephant will bolt and head in the direction where it believes the nearest food and water sources to be

consts.name: wmbHorseLoadRestTurns
consts.comment: an overloaded horse must be rested for at least one turn

consts.name: wmbHorseLoadTravelTurns
consts.comment: the overloaded-horse rest interval: after six turns of travel

consts.name: wmbHorseBitPct
consts.comment: the bit of food or water is one-half of a man's daily ration

consts.name: wmbHorseLamePct
consts.comment: there is a 2 percent chance (a roll of 01 or 02 on percentile dice) for every eight hours of travel through rugged or very rugged terrain that a horse will pull up lame, or stumble over an obstacle and become injured

consts.name: wmbHorseLameHours
consts.comment: the lame-or-injured check interval: every eight hours of rugged or very rugged travel

consts.name: wmbDraftLamePct
consts.comment: the chance is only 1 percent (roll of 01) for a draft horse

consts.name: wmbHorseRecoverHours
consts.comment: the 01-injury recovery: after 12 hours of rest

consts.name: wmbHorseFoodRations
consts.comment: a horse needs four rations of food (plants or grain) every day to remain at full strength

consts.name: wmbHorseWaterRations
consts.comment: a horse needs at least four rations of water every day to remain at full strength

consts.name: wmbMuleStubbornMin
consts.comment: the stubborn mule can stay rooted to one spot for half an hour or longer

consts.name: wmbMuleShortRationPct
consts.comment: a mule can be kept on three-fourths normal rations before suffering any adverse effects

consts.name: wmbMuleShortRationDays
consts.comment: the mule tolerates its reduced rations for as many as three consecutive days

consts.name: wmbPonyLamePct
consts.comment: a pony's chance of going lame is 2 percent for every eight hours spent traversing rugged or very rugged terrain

consts.name: wmbPonyLameHours
consts.comment: the pony lame check interval: every eight hours

consts.name: wmbPonyRations
consts.comment: a pony must have three rations of food or water per day

consts.name: wmbRamMaxTempF
consts.comment: they will not willingly stay in any area where the temperature regularly goes higher than 70 degrees

consts.name: wmbRamFoodRations
consts.comment: a giant ram or giant ewe needs six rations of food per day

consts.name: wmbRamWaterRations
consts.comment: a giant ram or giant ewe needs four rations of water per day

consts.name: wmbRamHotWaterRations
consts.comment: in an area where the daily high temperature exceeds 50 degrees, the animal needs six rations of water instead of only four

consts.name: wmbRamHotTempF
consts.comment: the daily-high threshold that raises the giant ram's water requirement: 50 degrees

consts.name: wmbSheepPerHandler
consts.comment: as a rule one character (mounted or afoot) can only control six sheep on the move

consts.name: wmbSheepStepPerHandler
consts.comment: the additional-handler step: every six sheep or fraction thereof

consts.name: wmbSheepUnsupervisedPct
consts.comment: if a flock is moved while not properly supervised, there is a 50 percent chance per hour of travel that the entire flock will develop a mind of its own and head in a random direction - which may be, but probably will not be, the direction they were supposed to go

consts.name: wmbSheepMaxTempF
consts.comment: the sheep temperature ceiling: 70 degrees

consts.name: wmbSheepFoodRations
consts.comment: a sheep needs two rations of food (plants) to remain at full strength

consts.name: wmbSheepWaterRations
consts.comment: a sheep needs two rations of water to remain at full strength

consts.name: wmbYakMaxTempF
consts.comment: a yak can only be used in arctic or subarctic climates where the temperature does not climb above 30 degrees

consts.name: wmbYakFoodRations
consts.comment: a yak needs six rations of food per day to remain at full strength

consts.name: wmbYakWaterRations
consts.comment: a yak needs four rations of water per day to remain at full strength

consts.name: wmbT42AnimalCount
consts.comment: the Table 42 row count: ape-gorilla, bear-brown, camel-any, dog-sled, donkey, elephant-any, horse-draft, horse-wild, horse-other, mule, pony, ram-giant, sheep, yak - in that order

consts.name: wmbReactDie
consts.comment: when an animal is exposed to one of the Table 42 conditions, the Dungeon Master rolls 1d12 to ascertain the animal's reaction

consts.name: wmbReactCalmRounds
consts.comment: the window to calm or control an excited animal before its behavior worsens: within two rounds

consts.name: wmbReactPanicDice
consts.comment: the panicked animal is utterly uncontrollable by normal nonmagical means: 2d3 turns - the dice count

consts.name: wmbReactPanicDie
consts.comment: the panicked-uncontrollable duration die: 2d3 turns

consts.name: wmbFireBonfireMiNum
consts.comment: the large-blaze sensing distance: one-quarter mile - the numerator

consts.name: wmbFireBonfireMiDen
consts.comment: the large-blaze sensing distance: one-quarter mile - the denominator

consts.name: wmbFireConflagrationMi
consts.comment: the forest-fire-scale conflagration sensing distance: one mile

consts.name: wmbCalmNonprofPct
consts.comment: a character without proficiency in animal handling has a straight 20 percent chance of bringing an excited animal under control

consts.name: wmbCalmNonprofAttempts
consts.comment: a nonproficient character can only make two such attempts on the same animal, in successive rounds if desired

consts.name: wmbCalmMovePct
consts.comment: the stationary excited animal splits evenly: a 50 percent chance of each of remaining still or beginning to move

consts.name: wmbCalmAgitatedMod
consts.comment: the calming Proficiency Check is made with a +2 modifier to the die roll if the animal is agitated

consts.name: wmbCalmPanickedMod
consts.comment: the calming Proficiency Check is made with a +4 modifier to the die roll if the animal is panicked

bools.name: wmbCatalogIntro
bools.comment: a large variety of land-based animals can be used by characters as mounts and beasts of burden; nearly every type has a distinctive personality with traits that set it apart, making the animal relatively more or less useful in certain circumstances

bools.name: wmbCatalogCrossRefs
bools.comment: the movement rates and encumbrance capacities of the most often employed mounts and pack animals are described in the section on Encumbrance and Movement; this section gives their behavior, proper care and feeding, and the special factors characters may have to contend with when employing a certain animal

bools.name: wmbApeHighestInt
bools.comment: among the animals considered here the gorilla has the highest intelligence rating

bools.name: wmbApeBefriendTrain
bools.comment: a gorilla that can be befriended (naturally or magically) can be trained to follow simple instructions as well as transport equipment

bools.name: wmbApePointMan
bools.comment: a gorilla might be made to serve as the point man on an expedition, avoiding putting a character in jeopardy by requiring him to serve in that capacity

bools.name: wmbApeNotStealthy
bools.comment: a gorilla is not capable of moving with any great degree of stealth; a group containing one or more of these animals has a smaller-than-normal chance of being able to surprise another character or creature

bools.name: wmbApeProhibitedDeserts
bools.comment: forced to remain in a colder area or to move on any prohibited terrain, a gorilla becomes lethargic or aggressive and deserts the group at its first opportunity - perhaps taking along anything it was carrying (certainly so if the equipment is strapped to its body)

bools.name: wmbBearNeedsMagic
bools.comment: this animal cannot reliably be used to carry anyone or anything unless it is magically befriended and trained

bools.name: wmbBearNonmagicRevert
bools.comment: a bear can be domesticated and trained by non-magical means, but there is a chance per month thereafter that it will revert to its natural temperament and head back for the wild

bools.name: wmbBearTerrain
bools.comment: a bear used as a mount or pack animal will traverse any kind of terrain except for swamp and desert

bools.name: wmbBearClaws
bools.comment: its nonretractable claws make it sure-footed on most terrain but prevent it from negotiating smooth slopes that are severely or moderately inclined

bools.name: wmbBearOmnivorous
bools.comment: a bear is omnivorous; it can and will eat anything that a man can eat

bools.name: wmbCamelDromedaryDesert
bools.comment: for game purposes the single-humped camel (the dromedary) is the variety exclusively suited for hot desert regions

bools.name: wmbCamelNoMove
bools.comment: the dromedary cannot move in mountains, forests or swamps at all

bools.name: wmbCamelNoSevereSlope
bools.comment: the dromedary cannot negotiate a severe slope of any sort in any other terrain

bools.name: wmbCamelBactrian
bools.comment: the double-humped camel (the bactrian) has smaller feet than the dromedary and is able to negotiate rocky or mountainous terrain; it can also be used in the desert, but like its one-humped cousin it will balk at being taken into a forest or a swamp

bools.name: wmbCamelSecondWeekHalf
bools.comment: during the second week of such deprivation a camel's carrying capacity is reduced to one-half of normal

bools.name: wmbCamelProportionate
bools.comment: reduce these amounts proportionately if it has been less than two weeks since the camel's last meal

bools.name: wmbDogColdAdapted
bools.comment: the animals that pull a sled and its contents over snowy or smooth terrain are hardy and dependable, but the sled dog is physiologically suited to cold weather

bools.name: wmbDogRation
bools.comment: a sled dog must be fed at least as much as a man's ration of food and water every day to maintain full strength; water is free for the taking in the form of snow

bools.name: wmbDogCannibalDetail
bools.comment: explorers have avoided this grisly occurrence by killing one of the dogs before the others get around to it - a tactic for only the direst circumstances

bools.name: wmbDogFourDogRates
bools.comment: a four-dog sled moves at 9 inches with a normal load and 6 inches with a full load on normal terrain, or 3 inches with a normal load over rugged terrain

bools.name: wmbDogSingleDog
bools.comment: a sled pulled by a single dog cannot move over rugged terrain at all, and has rates of 6 and 3 inches on normal terrain

bools.name: wmbDonkeySameAsMule
bools.comment: the abilities and characteristics of a donkey are generally the same as those of a mule, except for differences noted in this section and in the section on Movement and Encumbrance

bools.name: wmbEleTrainedOnly
bools.comment: a trained elephant is the only kind anyone should attempt to ride or use, and it will generally respond only to particular verbal commands taught to it by the trainer - do not buy an elephant unless the command words are included in the price

bools.name: wmbEleNoSlope
bools.comment: an elephant will not travel up or down a mountain or any severe slope; elephants can negotiate mountainous terrain only if a relatively level pass exists between the peaks

bools.name: wmbEleForageSlower
bools.comment: in an environment where it can forage for itself along the way, an elephant will eat its fill of food (plants) while traveling - but it will move slower when doing so

bools.name: wmbHorseFragile
bools.comment: perhaps the most numerous, and certainly one of the most fragile, beasts of burden available to the adventuring character

bools.name: wmbHorseStaminaException
bools.comment: the horse is an exception to the general stamina rules of the Encumbrance and Movement section: in addition to requiring rest after traveling for a number of hours, any horse carrying more than its normal load must be rested after its turns of travel

bools.name: wmbHorseRestBit
bools.comment: to provide the most benefit, the rest stop should include a bit of food and water - a bit to a horse is one-half of a man's daily ration - and most or all of the animal's load should be taken off its back, even if only for a few minutes

bools.name: wmbHorseLameSusceptible
bools.comment: all mounts and pack animals can go lame or become unable to travel through injury, but a horse is particularly susceptible to this problem

bools.name: wmbHorseLameTemporary
bools.comment: if the dice roll is 01, the horse is injured and cannot immediately move farther, but it will recover after its hours of rest

bools.name: wmbHorseLamePermanent
bools.comment: if the dice roll is 02, the horse is permanently injured and can no longer be used to carry a burden

bools.name: wmbMuleHardier
bools.comment: a mule is a much hardier and stronger animal than a horse, but its advantage is offset by its slower movement rate over normal terrain; it travels over rugged and very rugged terrain at least as well as a horse, and because its carrying capacity is greater than that of most horses it is often the best animal to take on a journey through potentially treacherous terrain

bools.name: wmbMuleStubborn
bools.comment: mules are particularly noted for their capriciousness, which usually manifests itself in stubbornness: a mule may remain rooted to one spot for half an hour or longer

bools.name: wmbMuleStrengthCheck
bools.comment: a character can get a stubborn mule to move without causing injury to the animal by making a Strength Check, but the mule will only take a few steps before pulling up short again - a long succession of Strength Checks gets very tedious, and it is usually better simply to wait until the mule decides to move again

bools.name: wmbMuleSameAsHorse
bools.comment: a mule normally needs the same amount of food (plants or grain) and water as a horse does, except for its reduced-ration tolerance

bools.name: wmbPonyLikeHorse
bools.comment: most of the general statements about horses apply to ponies as well

bools.name: wmbPonyMountainBred
bools.comment: ponies can be specially bred for traveling in mountainous terrain, and in such a case the Dungeon Master may allow them to move through such areas at a faster rate than what is given in the section on Encumbrance and Movement

bools.name: wmbRamChargeTrained
bools.comment: either a giant ram (the male) or a giant ewe (the female) can be used as a mount or pack animal, but rams are generally preferred because they can be trained to charge an opponent on command

bools.name: wmbRamHabitat
bools.comment: these animals are only found naturally in hills or mountains in a temperate or subarctic climate

bools.name: wmbRamPersuadedTerrain
bools.comment: as part of their domestication and training they can be persuaded to travel on flat, dry terrain except for deserts

bools.name: wmbRamNoForestSwamp
bools.comment: giant rams and ewes will not willingly enter forests or swamps

bools.name: wmbSheepPackUse
bools.comment: even though they are not normally thought of as pack animals, sheep can be useful for this purpose: each animal can carry a small load, and a small herd of two dozen has a greater carrying capacity than many larger animals have

bools.name: wmbSheepHerding
bools.comment: the animals' herding instinct, plus some effort on the part of the accompanying characters, will keep them in a cohesive group and headed in the desired direction

bools.name: wmbSheepNoProfNeeded
bools.comment: no special ability or proficiency is needed to shepherd a group of sheep

bools.name: wmbSheepExtraHandlers
bools.comment: for every additional six sheep (or fraction thereof) in the flock, another character (or a dog trained in sheepherding) is needed to help keep them in line

bools.name: wmbSheepClimate
bools.comment: sheep will travel in temperate or colder climates, or in any area where the temperature does not exceed 70 degrees; they will not willingly enter, or stay in, forests, deserts or swamps

bools.name: wmbSheepNondurable
bools.comment: a sheep being used to carry nondurable supplies (things that are used up along the way, such as food for characters, arrows, crossbow bolts) can itself be used for food when its usefulness as a carrier is over

bools.name: wmbYakLikeRam
bools.comment: the yak is similar in most respects to a giant ram, except that its range of terrain and temperature is even smaller

bools.name: wmbYakMountainous
bools.comment: a yak can only be used in mountainous terrain

bools.name: wmbYakNormalTerrainNote
bools.comment: normal terrain occurring inside a mountainous area - flat, or sloping at only a very gentle incline - does not preclude the use of a yak, since the animal is still being kept inside a mountainous area

bools.name: wmbIndivBitPlayers
bools.comment: the animals that accompany a party can be bit players in the adventure: taken for granted, they will serve capably and uncomplainingly as long as you keep them fed, do not work them too hard, and do not try to take them where they cannot go

bools.name: wmbIndivNpcTreatment
bools.comment: taking things one small step further, it is not difficult and can be very interesting to treat each mount and pack animal as a unique sort of non-player character

bools.name: wmbIndivFormerOwner
bools.comment: a character can sometimes gain valuable information about an animal from its former owner (assuming the seller is reputable and honest); the Dungeon Master can use this to modify the general characteristics of the animal, taking into account its individuality

bools.name: wmbIndivSurefootedExample
bools.comment: the sure-footed example: a horse known to be very sure-footed but hating to get his feet wet is less susceptible to going lame and might move slightly faster in rugged or very rugged terrain than a normal horse - but it will not willingly enter a swamp or ford a river, and if forced it will either travel slower than normal, or might balk or even panic

bools.name: wmbIndivWildTrial
bools.comment: if an animal is captured in the wild, trial and error is the only way for a character to find out what its personality is like, short of magical means such as a speak with animals spell

bools.name: wmbIndivControlledExposure
bools.comment: if unsure how an animal will react in a certain situation, expose the creature to the situation under controlled circumstances - lead it into a stream just before breaking camp when it is calm and well rested, not while being chased by hobgoblins across a ford

bools.name: wmbIndivCalmStability
bools.comment: animals appreciate calmness and stability; they do not like being exposed to unpleasant or potentially harmful conditions, do not like being startled or upset by something they did not expect, and may behave irrationally when something out of the ordinary happens

bools.name: wmbIndivFireFear
bools.comment: all normal (non-fantastic) animals have an instinctive fear of fire

bools.name: wmbIndivWeatherSense
bools.comment: to varying degrees, animals have an innate ability to sense when a drastic change in the weather is about to occur

bools.name: wmbIndivStartleNoiseSmell
bools.comment: all of them can be startled by a loud noise, or bothered by an unpleasant smell

bools.name: wmbIndivAcuteSenses
bools.comment: as a general rule an animal's sense of smell and sense of hearing are more acute than those of a human or demihuman: when an animal appears nervous or excited, it may be because it has perceived something that the character riding or leading it has not yet noticed

bools.name: wmbIndivNotCapricious
bools.comment: most animals are not intelligent enough to be capricious; when they seem to be bothered, it is a good bet that they are not acting that way just because they feel like it

bools.name: wmbReactNoticed
bools.comment: a result equal to or greater than the leftmost number means the animal has noticed the condition, sometimes before any characters have perceived it: noticeably nervous or excited, pacing or prancing skittishly and making vocal sounds for no apparent reason

bools.name: wmbReactAgitated
bools.comment: a result equal to or greater than the second number means the animal may become agitated: unless a character takes steps to calm or control it within two rounds, the abnormal behavior becomes more pronounced - it will refuse to move, or proceed very cautiously, if forced to travel toward the threat it perceives

bools.name: wmbReactTrustInstinct
bools.comment: if the character has not figured out what is bothering the animal by the time it becomes agitated, it is a good idea to trust the animal's instinct: do not force it to move in a direction it does not want to go, or better yet allow it to move in a direction of its choosing

bools.name: wmbReactPanicked
bools.comment: a result equal to or greater than the third number, if one is given, means the animal may become panicked: unless calmed and brought under control within two rounds of when it became excited, it will behave in a manner that seems utterly irrational but is motivated by self-preservation, doing everything in its power to move away from the perceived threat

bools.name: wmbReactPanicDuration
bools.comment: the panicked animal remains uncontrollable for the 2d3 turns or until it has moved sufficiently far away from the threat, whichever amount of time is greater

bools.name: wmbReactNoThirdNoPanic
bools.comment: if no third number is given in the Table 42 entry, the animal will not become panicked from that condition

bools.name: wmbFireGreatest
bools.comment: fire frightens an animal more than any other force or source of energy found in nature; even an animal that has never seen a fire knows instinctively that flames are to be avoided - this also applies to non-flaming natural heat sources such as flowing lava, and to magical fire that produces heat, but not to a flamelike phenomenon that does not give off heat, such as a faerie fire spell

bools.name: wmbFireCampfireHabit
bools.comment: an animal can become accustomed to the nearby presence of a small fire if it learns to associate the fire with something good - tie the horse, build the campfire, then feed it or let it graze; after a few days of the sequence it may actually look forward to the evening fire

bools.name: wmbFireNeverComfortableLarge
bools.comment: no animal will ever be comfortable in the vicinity of any blaze larger than a normal campfire, regardless of how many times it is exposed to a large fire without being harmed

bools.name: wmbFireSensing
bools.comment: an animal may sense the presence of a bonfire or similarly large blaze - a burning building, a wall of fire spell - from as far away as one-quarter mile, and an even larger conflagration such as a forest fire or grass fire covering a large area from one mile, usually long before a character is aware the fire is nearby

bools.name: wmbWeatherSenseDetail
bools.comment: weather changes are noticeable to animals before the signs come within sight range of characters; an animal becomes excited when it senses any upcoming significant change, such as an approaching moderate rainstorm, but becomes agitated or panicked only if the change is very drastic and very imminent, such as an approaching lightning storm or tornado - extremely unusual behavior with no other obvious cause may mean hazardous weather is on the way

bools.name: wmbNoiseDetail
bools.comment: noise in this context is a sound loud enough and sharp enough to startle a nearby animal - a shout, a crack of thunder, the clang of a sword on a metal shield; an animal can become accustomed to a particular noise through frequent exposure, such as simulated combat complete with whoops, growls and clangs during training to prevent panic in melee

bools.name: wmbSharpHearing
bools.comment: an animal with exceptionally sensitive hearing will not become agitated or panicked when it detects a sound inaudible to its rider or owner, though it may become excited - a character with proficiency in animal lore might ascertain the nature of what the animal is reacting to

bools.name: wmbOdorDetail
bools.comment: odor will only produce an extreme reaction when the scent is strong and pungent, which usually means it can be smelled by a character as well; an animal with an exceptionally sensitive nose will not become agitated or panicked by an odor too faint for a character to perceive, unless the animal associates the odor with something harmful or unpleasant

bools.name: wmbOtherQuirks
bools.comment: the other column covers a wide range of stimuli - some little thing that goes unnoticed by characters and most animals but excites, agitates or panics a certain animal: a quirk that personalizes it, like the donkey that plods through a mosquito-infested swamp oblivious to bugs on its snout but flies into a bucking frenzy when one gets inside its ear, the elephant that refuses a shallow stream unless relieved of its entire burden, the lead sled dog that refuses light snow crust and thereby saves the party on thin ice, and the bear-scarred horse that will not tolerate a bear as a pack animal but sounds the alarm long before a wild bear approaches the campsite

bools.name: wmbCalmAnyoneTries
bools.comment: any character can try to soothe an animal that has become excited

bools.name: wmbCalmProfChance
bools.comment: someone with proficiency in animal handling has a reasonably good chance of calming the beast, assuming he has an above-average wisdom score

bools.name: wmbCalmProfEveryRound
bools.comment: a proficient character can make a new attempt every round if his previous attempt failed, or if more than one animal is excited

bools.name: wmbCalmOnlyMove
bools.comment: any character who attempts to calm an animal can take no other action in the same round except for movement, if necessary

bools.name: wmbCalmMotionState
bools.comment: if an animal is in motion when it becomes excited, it will remain in motion; if it is stationary, it will either remain still or begin moving, with an even chance of each occurrence

bools.name: wmbCalmSootheMoving
bools.comment: a character attempting to soothe a moving animal must either be riding it or be able to keep up with it as it moves along

bools.name: wmbCalmAgitatedProfOnly
bools.comment: if an animal becomes agitated or panicked, only a character with proficiency in animal handling has any chance of calming the beast

bools.name: wmbCalmReexcite
bools.comment: even if an animal is calmed, there is no guarantee it will not become excited again in the following round: if the condition that upset it is still evident to the animal, it may become excited all over again and require the constant attention of an animal handler to prevent it from doing something drastic

bools.name: wmbUnderstandProf
bools.comment: a character with proficiency in animal lore has the ability - partially innate, partially learned - to make at least an educated guess about why an animal is acting a certain way, even if the reason for its behavior is not obvious to the character

bools.name: wmbUnderstandNonprof
bools.comment: a character without the proficiency may still draw logical conclusions from what his physical senses tell him - thunder and a skittish horse - but he can guess and cannot always know what is bothering his mount

bools.name: wmbUnderstandCertainty
bools.comment: in contrast, the proficient character can usually determine the cause with certainty, which also has the effect of ruling out any other possibilities

tables.name: wmbT42
col_comments: fire: the noticed threshold, equal to or greater than on 1d12
fire: the panicked threshold - 13 is the sentinel, an impossible 1d12 result standing for the bare trailing slash, meaning no third number given so the animal will not become panicked
weather: the panicked threshold or the sentinel
noise: the panicked threshold or the sentinel
odor: the panicked threshold or the sentinel
other: the panicked threshold or the sentinel
tables.audit_comment: the Table 42 reactions grid: each entry is two or three numbers, each a possible result on a roll of 1d12 when the animal is exposed to the condition - the leftmost is noticed, the second agitated, the third panicked; the sentinel 13 marks the cells whose printed entry ends in a bare trailing slash with no third number, meaning the animal will not become panicked from that condition

examples.note: the Table 42 band order: noticed strictly below agitated and agitated strictly below panicked for the ape, bear, camel, dog and donkey rows across all five conditions
examples.expr: m['wmbT42FireN'](0) >= m['wmbT42FireA'](0) or m['wmbT42WeatherA'](0) >= m['wmbT42WeatherP'](0) or m['wmbT42NoiseN'](1) >= m['wmbT42NoiseA'](1) or m['wmbT42OdorA'](2) >= m['wmbT42OdorP'](2) or m['wmbT42OtherN'](3) >= m['wmbT42OtherA'](3) or m['wmbT42FireA'](4) >= m['wmbT42FireP'](4)

examples.note: the sentinel placement: the mule row carries the bare-trailing-slash sentinel in exactly its fire, weather, noise and odor panic cells, and the ram odor cell, never in a noticed or agitated cell
examples.expr: m['wmbT42FireP'](9) != 13 or m['wmbT42WeatherP'](9) != 13 or m['wmbT42NoiseP'](9) != 13 or m['wmbT42OdorP'](9) != 13 or m['wmbT42OtherP'](9) != 12 or m['wmbT42OdorP'](11) != 13 or m['wmbT42FireN'](9) == 13 or m['wmbT42FireA'](11) == 13

examples.note: the ape and elephant no-panic cells: weather and noise end in the sentinel with their exact threshold values
examples.expr: m['wmbT42WeatherN'](0) != 6 or m['wmbT42WeatherP'](0) != 13 or m['wmbT42NoiseN'](0) != 8 or m['wmbT42NoiseP'](0) != 13 or m['wmbT42WeatherN'](5) != 7 or m['wmbT42NoiseN'](5) != 8 or m['wmbT42WeatherP'](5) != 13 or m['wmbT42NoiseP'](5) != 13

examples.note: the donkey uniform row: every condition shares agitated 10 and panicked 12 with noticed 4 or 6
examples.expr: m['wmbT42FireN'](4) != 4 or m['wmbT42WeatherN'](4) != 6 or m['wmbT42FireA'](4) != 10 or m['wmbT42WeatherA'](4) != 10 or m['wmbT42NoiseA'](4) != 10 or m['wmbT42OdorA'](4) != 10 or m['wmbT42OtherA'](4) != 10 or m['wmbT42OtherP'](4) != 12

examples.note: the boundary rows: the bear fire band 4/8/10, the horse-wild other band 5/9/12, and the yak fire band 7/10/12
examples.expr: m['wmbT42FireN'](1) != 4 or m['wmbT42FireA'](1) != 8 or m['wmbT42FireP'](1) != 10 or m['wmbT42OtherN'](7) != 5 or m['wmbT42OtherA'](7) != 9 or m['wmbT42OtherP'](7) != 12 or m['wmbT42FireN'](13) != 7 or m['wmbT42FireA'](13) != 10

examples.note: the animal count and the die: fourteen animals in the grid, the reaction roll on 1d12, with the calm window of two rounds and the panic duration of 2d3 turns
examples.expr: m['wmbT42AnimalCount']() != 14 or m['wmbReactDie']() != 12 or m['wmbReactCalmRounds']() != 2 or m['wmbReactPanicDice']() != 2 or m['wmbReactPanicDie']() != 3

examples.note: the fire sensing distances: the large blaze at one-quarter mile and the conflagration at one mile
the ape needs and risks: the 1-in-6 surprise cut, the 50-degree floor, the 50 percent lethargic-or-aggressive split, the 10x food and 8x water multipliers, and the 25 percent foraging failure chance
examples.expr: m['wmbApeSurpriseMin']() != 1 or m['wmbApeMinTempF']() != 50 or m['wmbApeDesertChancePct']() != 50 or m['wmbApeFoodMult']() != 10 or m['wmbApeWaterMult']() != 8 or m['wmbApeForageFailPct']() != 25

examples.note: the bear and camel needs: the bear 30 percent reversion with 8x food and 6x water, the camel 50-degree floor with two-day weakness and the two-week fast halving capacity at the 10x and 20x empty refueling
examples.expr: m['wmbBearRevertPct']() != 30 or m['wmbBearFoodMult']() != 8 or m['wmbBearWaterMult']() != 6 or m['wmbCamelMinTempF']() != 50 or m['wmbCamelWeakDays']() != 2 or m['wmbCamelDeprivedCapPct']() != 50 or m['wmbCamelEmptyFoodMult']() != 10 or m['wmbCamelEmptyWaterMult']() != 20

examples.note: the sled dog team: the 40-degree ceiling with 2-3 inches of snow, the two-day cannibalism bar at 50 percent, the seven-dog optimum with the 200 and 300 gold piece losses and the 3-inch rate cut per three dogs short
examples.expr: m['wmbDogMaxTempF']() != 40 or m['wmbDogSnowMinIn']() != 2 or m['wmbDogSnowMaxIn']() != 3 or m['wmbDogStarveDays']() != 2 or m['wmbDogCannibalPct']() != 50 or m['wmbDogTeamFull']() != 7 or m['wmbDogNormalLossGp']() != 200 or m['wmbDogMaxLossGp']() != 300 or m['wmbDogRateStepDogs']() != 3 or m['wmbDogRateLossIn']() != 3

examples.note: the sled rates: the four-dog 9/6/3 and the single-dog 6/3 with the rugged ban
examples.expr: m['wmbDogFourNormalIn']() != 9 or m['wmbDogFourFullIn']() != 6 or m['wmbDogFourRuggedIn']() != 3 or m['wmbDogOneNormalIn']() != 6 or m['wmbDogOneFullIn']() != 3

examples.note: the elephant needs: the 50-degree floor, the 3-inch forage slowdown, the fifty and thirty rations, and the bolt check at 50 percent every six hours after two unfed days
examples.expr: m['wmbEleMinTempF']() != 50 or m['wmbEleForageSlowIn']() != 3 or m['wmbEleFoodRations']() != 50 or m['wmbEleWaterRations']() != 30 or m['wmbEleBoltDays']() != 2 or m['wmbEleBoltCheckHours']() != 6 or m['wmbEleBoltPct']() != 50

examples.note: the horse rules: the overloaded one-turn rest per six turns, the bit at half a man's daily ration, the 2 percent lame chance per eight rugged hours (1 percent for the draft), the 12-hour recovery, and the four food and four water rations
examples.expr: m['wmbHorseLoadRestTurns']() != 1 or m['wmbHorseLoadTravelTurns']() != 6 or m['wmbHorseBitPct']() != 50 or m['wmbHorseLamePct']() != 2 or m['wmbHorseLameHours']() != 8 or m['wmbDraftLamePct']() != 1 or m['wmbHorseRecoverHours']() != 12 or m['wmbHorseFoodRations']() != 4 or m['wmbHorseWaterRations']() != 4

examples.note: the mule and pony: the half-hour stubborn root with the three-fourths rations for three days, and the pony 2 percent lame per eight hours with three rations daily
examples.expr: m['wmbMuleStubbornMin']() != 30 or m['wmbMuleShortRationPct']() != 75 or m['wmbMuleShortRationDays']() != 3 or m['wmbPonyLamePct']() != 2 or m['wmbPonyLameHours']() != 8 or m['wmbPonyRations']() != 3

examples.note: the ram, sheep and yak: the ram 70-degree ceiling with 6 food and 4 water rising to 6 above the 50-degree daily high, the sheep six per handler with the 50 percent per hour unsupervised bolt and the 70-degree ceiling, and the yak 30-degree ceiling
examples.expr: m['wmbRamMaxTempF']() != 70 or m['wmbRamFoodRations']() != 6 or m['wmbRamWaterRations']() != 4 or m['wmbRamHotWaterRations']() != 6 or m['wmbRamHotTempF']() != 50 or m['wmbSheepPerHandler']() != 6 or m['wmbSheepUnsupervisedPct']() != 50 or m['wmbSheepMaxTempF']() != 70 or m['wmbYakMaxTempF']() != 30 or m['wmbYakFoodRations']() != 6 or m['wmbYakWaterRations']() != 4

examples.note: the calming rules: the straight 20 percent nonproficient chance with two attempts, the 50-50 motion split, and the +2 agitated and +4 panicked proficiency modifiers
examples.expr: m['wmbCalmNonprofPct']() != 20 or m['wmbCalmNonprofAttempts']() != 2 or m['wmbCalmMovePct']() != 50 or m['wmbCalmAgitatedMod']() != 2 or m['wmbCalmPanickedMod']() != 4

examples.note: the calming modifiers scale with the condition: the panicked modifier double the agitated modifier

pushed 1ac64e0..c11cbe1), the WSG FATIGUE CHAPTER
slice, printed pp. 87-89 - CLOSING the wilderness
combat chapter with its dismount tail and LANDING
the full fatigue and exhaustion chapter. Pinned as
rules/wsgfatig.h with the include after
wsgfight.h at line 194 (prefix wft - free on the
first probe), 120 inlines: 65 consts + 55 bools in
five sections - the chapter opener, the p. 87
dismount tail, Characters, Land-based mounts and
pack animals, Flying mounts. The R488 "cut"
settled as a column wrap WITHIN p. 87, not a page
cut: the right column carries "Dungeon Master may
allow a character with proficiency in riding the
mount to leap from its back and land safely on
the ground" - the dismount section was complete
and only the connective pin rode to this round,
CLOSING the combat chapter. Characters: the
4-turn strenuous risk (over-full movement, melee,
climbing, swimming against a current, severe
encumbrance), the 2-turn rest to avoid it, the
6-turn first Constitution Check, 5 more turns on
success with the interval shrinking 1 turn per
success to a minimum of 1, fatigue dropping every
ability score except comeliness by 2 until 2
consecutive hours of rest (the Str 18 / Con 18 /
Wis 14 examples: +1 to-hit lost and +2 damage to
+1, 2 hp per hit die at a temporary 16, both
bonus 1st-level spells lost with a spell-failure
chance at an effective 12), checks reading the
current score, a further -2 on attacks and saves,
the per-turn Con Check while continuing with
failure meaning exhaustion (another -2 and no
voluntary action except when failure to move
risks death), the 1-hour rest plus a check to
leave only fatigue then 2 more hours, and the
rest-while-carried and rest-tied-to-mount rules.
Land-based mounts: 2 days without food and water
or 3 days short rations fatigues, full ration plus
8 hours rest recovers, overwork recovery 12 hours
plus 2 per hour overworked (the 3-hour horse
resting 18), fatigued half movement with
1-round-per-turn bursts, the 3-inch terrain bar
(the loaded horse and the camel in very rugged
ground), 2 armor class places worse (7 to 9),
only the animal-handling proficient calming the
excited fatigued animal and only at the
nonproficient chance, the cumulative 20% per hour
exhaustion chance with the 1-hour reset, the
collapse ladder 25/50/75, the oblivious exhausted
animal that neither panics nor defends itself,
the flat 50% death chance within 1d4 hours, and
the 1d6-3 trauma drain through the 8-hour
critical period with the 2-per-hour regain.
Flying mounts: never exhausted; the stamina first
number is the safe flying time (reduced when
heavily loaded), past it a 1d10 per turn with the
fatigue chance 10 minus the rest number (the
black dragon 24/6 fatiguing on 1-4), flying and
rest not in full blocks (the 30-turn window with
24 aloft and 6 rest; the 7-turn last flight
risking fatigue), exceeding then landing demanding
a full rest, fatigue dropping the rate to
two-thirds with 10 yards of altitude lost per
round, the same-turn safe landing within 100
yards, past that the second-turn steep dive with
1d2 buffet damage per 10 yards dived halved for
airborne-riding proficiency or secure strapping,
the unstrapped rider thrown for 11-40 (3d10+10),
and the 3-times post-fatigue rest refusal (18
turns for the dragon) unless self-preservation
dictates. THE SETTLE: two-way clean on the first
pass (the layout l d 4 / l d 6 / l d l O / l d 2
classes are 1d4 1d6 1d10 1d2; Constutition and
conscutive are book typos; tesseract confirms 24/6,
ladder, 0-3, 2 per hour and 20%/hour). One
